drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 68-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.85, creatinine 1.02-1.24, hemoglobin 13.6-13.8, platelets 199-201, sodium 138, wbc 9.6-9.8; vitals dbp 76-82, heart_rate 76-79, map 91-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-14, sbp 122-128, spo2 95-97, temp 36.6-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.47-1.68, hemoglobin 13.6-13.8, platelets 197-201, sodium 138, wbc 9.1-9.2; vitals dbp 76-79, heart_rate 76-80, map 92-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 120-128, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Hold lisinopril; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 68-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
